title: Realize compatible affine coherent cohomology as an etale module higher image
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, $E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For each affine etale $v:V\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], set $X_V=X\times_SV$, with projections $f_V:X_V\to V$ and $j_V:X_V\to X$, and $G_V=j_V^*G$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback]. Suppose given $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-linear bijections
$$e_v:H^q(X_V,G_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V,v^*E)$$
[pqf-def-cohomology], such that for every arrow $h:V'\to V$ between affine etale $S$-objects one has $e_{vh}\circ h_X^*=\rho_h\circ e_v$. Here $h_X:X_{V'}\to X_V$, $h_X^*$ is the module cohomology pullback with its canonical coefficient identification [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], and $\rho_h$ is the tensor-section restriction of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Use the common coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with the same sectionwise additive lift $L=\operatorname{ULift}$ on all associated etale sheaves. Then there is an isomorphism
$$\Phi:R^qf_*L(G_{\mathrm{et}})\xrightarrow{\sim}L(E_{\mathrm{et}})$$
of $L(\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}})$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The left hand side is computed in abelian sheaves, with the scalar action induced by multiplication by pullbacks of base functions, rather than an independently chosen action. Its normalization is as follows. Write $P(V)=H^q(X_{V,\mathrm{et}},L((G_V)_{\mathrm{et}}))$, and let $\iota_V:P(V)\to(R^qf_*L(G_{\mathrm{et}}))(V)$ be the canonical cohomology class map into the associated sheaf. For every affine $v$ and $x\in P(V)$,
$$\Phi_V(\iota_V(x))=\operatorname{ULift.up}\bigl(e_v(c^q_{X_V,G_V}(x))\bigr),$$
where $c^q$ is the simultaneous canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-qcoherent-cohomology-comparison-pullback]. Equivalently, for $z\in\operatorname{Hom}((f^{-1}\mathbf Z[V])[0],L(G_{\mathrm{et}})[0][q])$, with $\mathbf Z[V]$ the free abelian representable followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-natural-comparison], use $x=c_{\mathrm{raw}}(z)$ from [def-sbc-raw-restricted-cohomology-comparison-map] and use the canonical raw class in place of $\iota_V(x)$. The same $\Phi$ intertwines all local multiplications by all base sections on every etale object, including non-affine objects.

source.place: Tag 03Q8, label lemma-higher-direct-images, associated cohomology-presheaf construction; affine comparison and scalar normalization are the agent expansion of this construction using the existing simultaneous coherent comparison and dense affine-subsite interfaces.

proof.text: For every affine etale $v:V\to S$, base change makes $f_V:X_V\to V$ quasi-compact and separated. Thus $X_V$ is quasi-compact (apply quasi-compactness to the affine open $V$ itself), and is separated as a scheme because its base $V$ is affine. Pullback makes $G_V=j_V^*G$ quasi-coherent. These are exactly the geometric hypotheses of the simultaneous comparison, and they hold also for $V'$ in every arrow in the affine subsite; no quasi-compactness or separatedness of $S$ is required.

Write $F=L(G_{\mathrm{et}})$, $T=L(E_{\mathrm{et}})$ and $R=L(\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{et}})$. The base change $j_V$ of $v$ is etale. Inverse image along $j_V$ is restriction: on an etale $w:W\to X_V$ it evaluates $F$ on $j_Vw$. The module pullback composition isomorphism identifies $(j_Vw)^*G$ with $w^*G_V$, naturally in $w$. Hence $j_V^{-1}F=L((G_V)_{\mathrm{et}})$ with precisely the structural coefficient identification. Applying the same sectionwise lift to restrictions preserves these identities. In particular the presheaf in 03Q8 is the presheaf $P(V)=H^q(X_{V,\mathrm{et}},L((G_V)_{\mathrm{et}}))$ in the statement, with its actual restriction maps.

source.place: 03Q8 restricted coefficient; 03S2 restriction and tensor-pullback composition

proof.text: On the full etale site put $\widetilde P(V)=H^q(X_V,j_V^{-1}F)$, with cohomological restriction. The canonical cocycle class $\iota:\widetilde P\to R^qf_*F$ exhibits $R^qf_*F$ as its abelian sheafification. For arbitrary $V$, let $a\in R(V)$ act on $\widetilde P(V)$ by the cohomology endomorphism induced by multiplying $j_V^{-1}F$ by $f_V^*a$. The coefficient identities $(a+b)m=am+bm$, $(ab)m=a(bm)$ and $1m=m$ pass to cohomology, giving a module structure. Coefficient naturality of cohomology pullback (clause 3 of its functoriality theorem) carries that multiplication to multiplication by the restricted base function, so this is a presheaf of $R$-modules. Its module sheafification has underlying abelian sheaf $R^qf_*F$ by the module-sheafification interface. Its action is exactly the action induced by local multiplication specified in the item; it is not chosen through an eventual isomorphism with $T$.

source.place: Tag 03Q8, label lemma-higher-direct-images; module structure by Tag 03CY

proof.text:
For affine $v$ define $\alpha_V(x)=\operatorname{ULift.up}(e_v(c^q_{X_V,G_V}(x)))$. For $h:V'\to V$, comparison naturality and the given compatibility of $e$ give
$$\alpha_{V'}(h_X^*x)=\operatorname{ULift.up}(e_{vh}(h_X^*c^q_{X_V,G_V}(x)))=\rho_h(\alpha_V(x)).$$
Thus $\alpha:P|_{\mathrm{aff}}\to T|_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is an isomorphism of additive presheaves. For $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ put $b=f_V^*a$. Comparison intertwines the endomorphism multiplying by $b$, and module cohomology sends that endomorphism to scalar multiplication by $b$. The given $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-linearity of $e_v$ therefore gives $\alpha_V(\operatorname{ULift.up}(a)x)=\operatorname{ULift.up}(a)\alpha_V(x)$. Every lifted scalar has this form. This proves linearity for the action fixed in step 3.

source.place: Tag 03P2 canonical comparison, applied to arrows between affine etale base objects and to multiplication

proof.text: Give the full affine etale subcategory $\mathcal A\subset S_{\mathrm{et}}$ the induced sieve topology. Its inclusion is fully faithful. Every etale $W\to S$ is covered by affine opens, so the image-covering condition of the sieve dense-subsite comparison holds. Its local fullness and local faithfulness conditions hold with the maximal sieve, since the inclusion is full and faithful; its covering-detection condition is the definition of the induced topology. Apply that comparison in the common universe $u+1$ to obtain an equivalence on sheaves of $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$. This gives an abelian equivalence in the same universe: extend each underlying set sheaf, lift addition, zero and negation by full faithfulness, and check their identities after faithful restriction. Restriction preserves products since sheaf products are computed sectionwise. Thus the dense-subsite sheafification comparison applies to the actual abelian coefficients, without resizing them or assuming $S$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 04HR affine-cover route; sieve dense-subsite comparison in the common coefficient universe

proof.text: The restriction $T|_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a sheaf for the induced topology, by the equivalence of step 5; hence step 4 makes $P|_{\mathrm{aff}}$ a sheaf as well. Write $u:\mathcal A\to S_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the inclusion and $\eta=\iota:\widetilde P\to\widetilde P^\#=R^qf_*F$ for the sheafification unit; by step 2, $\widetilde P\circ u^{op}=P|_{\mathrm{aff}}$. The dense-subsite sheafification comparison gives isomorphisms $\theta_H:(H\circ u^{op})^\#\cong H^\#\circ u^{op}$, natural in the abelian presheaf $H$ on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$. Naturality for the morphism $\eta:\widetilde P\to\widetilde P^\#$ reads $\theta_{\widetilde P^\#}\circ(\eta\circ u^{op})^\#=(\eta^\#\circ u^{op})\circ\theta_{\widetilde P}$. Here $\eta^\#$ is invertible (the sheafification of a sheafification unit, by the universal property), so $(\eta\circ u^{op})^\#$ is invertible. But $\eta\circ u^{op}=\iota|_{\mathrm{aff}}:P|_{\mathrm{aff}}\to(R^qf_*F)|_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a morphism between sheaves on $\mathcal A$, whose sheafification units are invertible and natural; so $\iota|_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is conjugate to $(\iota|_{\mathrm{aff}})^\#$ and is invertible. No compatibility of $\theta$ with units is used. Consequently each affine $\iota_V:P(V)\to(R^qf_*F)(V)$ is invertible and the formula $\Phi_V=\alpha_V\iota_V^{-1}$ defines an isomorphism on restricted abelian sheaves. Full faithfulness of restriction uniquely extends it and its inverse to an abelian sheaf isomorphism $\Phi:R^qf_*F\to T$. The two inverse identities hold because they hold after faithful restriction.

source.place: Tag 04HR affine-subsite descent; canonical dense-subsite/sheafification adjunction comparison

proof.text: On every affine object the equation $\Phi_V\iota_V=\alpha_V$ is the defining equation of step 6. The unit $\iota$ is linear for the sheafified action of step 3; thus its inverse is linear on each affine object, as is $\alpha_V$ by step 4. For an arbitrary etale $W\to S$, a scalar $a\in R(W)$ and $s\in(R^qf_*F)(W)$, restrict the two sections $\Phi_W(as)$ and $a\Phi_W(s)$ to an affine open cover $\{V_i\to W\}$. On $V_i$ their values are $\Phi_{V_i}(a|_{V_i}s|_{V_i})$ and $a|_{V_i}\Phi_{V_i}(s|_{V_i})$, equal by affine linearity. Sheaf uniqueness makes the two original sections equal. This proves linearity on every etale object; the inverse is linear by applying the bijection $\Phi_W$ to the scalar identity.

source.place: Tag 03CY module sheafification, followed by the etale sheaf uniqueness axiom

proof.text:
For an affine $v$ and $x\in P(V)$, step 6 reads
$$\Phi_V(\iota_V(x))=\alpha_V(x)=\operatorname{ULift.up}(e_v(c^q_{X_V,G_V}(x))),$$
which is the requested normalization with the common coefficient lift. For a raw class $z$, the raw-class normalization lemma gives $\kappa_V(z)=\iota_V(c_{\mathrm{raw}}(z))$, with the actual constructed raw evaluation and canonical higher-image class map. Substitute $x=c_{\mathrm{raw}}(z)$ into the preceding equality. This yields exactly the equivalent raw formula and completes the isomorphism with all local scalar compatibilities.
